assumptions: The institution seeks an evolution of its existing identity rather than a rename or merger-level brand architecture change.
The identity should preserve valuable heritage only after that equity is identified through research.
Responsible change will be defined and substantiated by the institution before it becomes a public-facing claim.
Digital, signage, print and merchandise applications will initially be representative priority touchpoints rather than an exhaustive asset inventory.
Accessibility, inclusive communication and environmentally responsible production will be evaluation criteria.
Final technical specifications will be adapted to confirmed platforms, sites and vendors.

prediction.rationale: The brief calls for a strategy-led identity evolution rather than a standalone visual refresh. The workflow therefore establishes institutional meaning and a communicable design-process model before visual exploration, requires explicit direction selection, tests the chosen idea across the named media, and only then codifies and extends the system. Final delivery is excluded because the incomplete brief does not yet establish the approvals and production inputs required for a valid handoff.
stop_conditions: Do not begin concept exploration until positioning, priority audiences, brand architecture and heritage equities are approved.
Do not advance beyond direction selection without an explicit human or client decision.
Pause if the institution cannot approve or substantiate claims connecting its programs to responsible change.
Do not finalize the identity system until naming and trademark risks have been reviewed by the responsible legal party.
Do not prepare production masters for any touchpoint lacking final content, dimensions, platform requirements or vendor specifications.
Do not release signage or merchandise files without accessibility, safety, material, fabrication and licensing approvals.

workflow_steps.objective: Confirm institutional goals, audiences, scope, constraints, success measures, decision-makers and missing inputs.

Specify brand architecture, content hierarchy, touchpoint priorities, formats and requirements across digital, signage, print and merchandise.
Develop meaningfully different identity directions that express the approved strategy and process model.
Evaluate directions against agreed criteria and obtain an explicit client choice.
Test the selected direction in rough digital interfaces, signage, print and merchandise applications for clarity, accessibility and coherence.
Apply stakeholder and testing feedback while preserving approved strategic and conceptual decisions.
Codify the logo, typography, colour, graphic language, motion or interaction behavior and governance rules.
Extend the approved identity across prioritized institutional touchpoints and reusable templates.
Prepare technically valid masters for the confirmed digital, print, environmental and merchandise outputs.

Apply the approved system across the planned lesson set, reusable activity templates, instructional graphics, feedback states and supporting visual assets.
Validate linguistic accuracy, instructional alignment, accessibility, consistency and file completeness, then package the education content system for handoff.

workflow_steps.objective: Confirm business goal, recipients, contents, quantity, budget, timing, brand inputs, mandatory copy, distribution route, manufacturing constraints, approval owners and measurable success criteria.

Review Mid-Autumn cultural context, recipient expectations, relevant market conventions, competitor packaging, accessibility, sustainability opportunities and converter capabilities without deriving a style from the published reference.
Agree decision principles for cultural appropriateness, brand recognition, gifting impact, unboxing sequence, product protection, material efficiency, finish restraint and manufacturability.
Define responsibilities, approval gates, vendor engineering reviews, proof and sample rounds, test criteria, change control and release authority before design development.
Develop meaningfully different structural, opening, presentation, graphic and finish directions, each accompanied by indicative materials, risks, cost tier and production implications.
Compare concepts against the agreed principles, feasibility and budget, then obtain explicit client and manufacturer approval for one direction and its permitted refinements.

Engineer the selected package architecture, including dimensions, component hierarchy, insert retention, closure, board or substrate assumptions, tolerances, assembly, packing, stacking and transport requirements.
Define the edition-specific surface-art system—information hierarchy, typography, colour, imagery or motifs, placement and finish logic—within the supplied master-brand rules.
Create component-level cutting, creasing, folding, glue and artwork geometry based on the approved structure and the nominated manufacturer's technical standards.

Produce and assess structural mockups, product-fit samples, decorated prototypes and finish strike-offs; test opening, retention, assembly, stacking, transit protection, legibility and finish registration as applicable.
Resolve feedback and test findings in the approved direction, updating structure, artwork, materials and finishes while documenting any effects on cost, timing or feasibility.

Prepare preflighted manufacturing masters with separations, bleeds, overprints, spot colours, white ink, foil, emboss or deboss, varnish, coating and assembly specifications aligned to the approved vendor template.
